168.content: Download the Linux AppImage or build dualsense-updater from source with Rust, Qt 6, and KDE Kirigami.

175.content: Pre-built x86_64 AppImage releases and `.tar.gz` archives are available via the Download page (requiring safety acknowledgment) and on GitHub Releases.

176.content: Firmware inspection and updates operate over USB HID only. Connect your DualSense controller using a reliable USB-C data cable (not Bluetooth, and avoid unpowered USB hubs).

177.content: If your desktop environment does not already include KDE Frameworks 6 QML modules, install your distribution's Qt 6 Kirigami runtime package (for example `kirigami` / `qml6-module-org-kde-kirigami` and `qqc2-desktop-style`). When `org.kde.desktop` is unavailable, the application automatically falls back to Qt's `Fusion` style (or respects `QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE`).

185.content: All unit and integration tests across the 3-crate workspace (`dualsense-core`, `dualsense-ui`, and `dualsense-updater`) run headlessly without a display server or physical controller:

187.content: Unofficial, community-maintained Linux KDE Kirigami desktop application for inspecting and updating PlayStation DualSense firmware over USB HID.

190.content: **Unofficial Linux DualSense Firmware Updater** (`Azorimor/linux-dualsense-fw-updater`) is an unofficial, community-maintained Linux desktop utility built with Rust and KDE Kirigami (Qt 6) for inspecting DualSense controller hardware and flashing firmware updates over a wired USB connection. It has **no affiliation, endorsement, or relation to Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation**.

191.content: This is an unofficial, community-maintained project with no affiliation, endorsement, or relation to Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation. Only use this software if you have no access to Sony's official PlayStation Accessories / DualSense firmware updater for Windows or a PlayStation 5 console. Firmware upgrades are auto-committed by the controller even if verify and finalize steps do not run, and flashing firmware can permanently damage or brick your controller. Use at your own risk.

192.content: The desktop GUI walks you through four stages while monitoring USB connection state:

193.content: **Controller** — Scans wired USB HID devices (`054c:0ce6` DualSense, `054c:0df2` DualSense Edge) and reads Feature Reports `0x20` and `0x81` to display current firmware version, build date, board revision (`BDM-*`), firmware series, and controller colorway.

194.content: **Firmware** — Either fetches Sony's official firmware catalog (`info.json`) for your detected hardware target (`0004`, `000B`, `000E`, or `0044`) or validates a local `.bin` image from disk.

195.content: **Review** — Compares current and target versions, warns if the controller is already up to date or if the target is untested (`DualSense Edge`), and requires explicit confirmation that firmware updates cannot be reversed.

196.content: **Update** — Streams downloads with safe pre-flash cancellation, writes firmware in 32 KiB blocks via Feature Report `0xF4`, polls status via `0xF5`, verifies, and finalizes.

197.content: **Automatic Board & Target Resolution**: Decodes hardware revision (`BDM-020` through `BDM-060R/M/X`) and firmware series to match the right Sony update target automatically.

198.content: **Live USB Disconnect Monitoring**: Polls USB device presence every 800 ms outside active flashing so unplugging a controller immediately resets to scan safely.

199.content: **Plain-English Error Recovery**: Translates low-level USB HID, catalog, and image validation failures into actionable recovery steps.

200.content: **Built-in Licenses Dialog**: Includes an in-app Licenses & Acknowledgments viewer covering GPL-3.0-or-later, MIT (nchie), and third-party Rust/Qt/KDE credits.

202.content: GPL-3.0-or-later license, original author attribution to nchie (MIT), and third-party open-source software credits.

210.content: Firmware update irreversibility, Linux udev rules for /dev/hidraw access, and common recovery guidance.

216.content: Missing Kirigami QML style at launch

217.content: **Updates are irreversible:** Once flashing begins, firmware upgrades are auto-committed by the DualSense controller even if verify and finalize steps do not run.

218.content: **Controller verification:** In practice, the DualSense bootloader validates the firmware image signature and target SoC before committing, so flashing a wrong target fails verification rather than bricking the hardware. However, **never** disconnect the USB cable while blocks are being written.

219.content: **Already up-to-date controllers:** A controller already running the target or a newer firmware version may reject commands past the start-update phase because Sony's firmware blocks downgrades and same-version re-flashing.

220.content: The update protocol implementation has only been tested on standard DualSense hardware. DualSense Edge (`0x0df2` / target `0044`) is explicitly flagged in the Review step before flashing.

221.content: On Linux, opening DualSense HID devices (`/dev/hidraw*`) without root privileges requires `uaccess` or read/write permissions for Sony's USB Vendor ID (`054c`).

222.content: Many desktop distributions already provide `hidraw` rules (for example via Steam or `systemd`), but if the updater reports a permission error when opening the controller, create `/etc/udev/rules.d/70-dualsense-updater.rules`:

223.content: Then reload `udev` rules and replug your controller:

224.content: Confirm you are using a **data-capable** USB-C cable (charge-only cables will power the controller without exposing HID endpoints).

225.content: Disconnect Bluetooth pairing or hold the PS button briefly / replug USB so the controller enumerates over USB HID.

226.content: Verify the kernel sees the HID device with `lsusb | grep 054c`.

227.content: Check whether the controller is already on the same or newer firmware version. Sony's firmware rejects downgrades and duplicate flashes past `StartUpdate`.

228.content: Ensure the selected `.bin` image matches your controller's target ID (`0004`, `000B`, `000E`, or `0044`).

229.content: If the app launches with minimal styling or logs QML module warnings, confirm `org.kde.kirigami` (KF6) is installed on your system. You can also test with `QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Fusion`.

231.content: DualSense and DualSense Edge USB IDs, BDM board revision decoding, Sony firmware targets, and colorway detection.

233.content: Board Revision to Sony Target Mapping

236.content: The updater inspects Feature Report `0x20` (`hw_info` and `fw_series`) along with the USB Product ID to determine your controller's mainboard revision and matching Sony firmware target.

237.content:
| Device         | USB Vendor ID | USB Product ID | Testing Status               |
| -------------- | ------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Sony DualSense | `0x054c`      | `0x0ce6`       | Tested on standard DualSense |

238.content:
| Device              | USB Vendor ID | USB Product ID | Testing Status                         |
| ------------------- | ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Sony DualSense Edge | `0x054c`      | `0x0df2`       | **Untested** (flagged before flashing) |

239.content: Board revision is decoded from `(hw_info >> 8) & 0xff` in Feature Report `0x20`:

240.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support                               |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0x03`        | `BDM-010`      | —        | **Unsupported** (not in Sony's PC update catalog) |

241.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x04`        | `BDM-020`      | `0004`         | Supported                |

242.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x05`        | `BDM-030`      | `0004`         | Supported                |

243.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x06`        | `BDM-040`      | `0004`         | Supported                |

244.content:
| Hardware Byte   | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| --------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x07` / `0x08` | `BDM-050`      | `000B`         | Supported                |

245.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x09`        | `BDM-060R`     | `000E`         | Supported                |

246.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x11`        | `BDM-060M`     | `000E`         | Supported                |

247.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `0x13`        | `BDM-060X`     | `000E`         | Supported                |

248.content:
| Hardware Byte | Board Revision   | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support            |
| ------------- | ---------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| PID `0x0df2`  | `DualSense Edge` | `0044`         | Supported in catalog (**Untested**) |

249.content: Launch-era `BDM-010` DualSense controllers are not supported by Sony's official PC firmware catalog (`info.json`). The application detects `BDM-010` and disables official catalog flashing for safety.

**Unofficial Linux DualSense Firmware Updater** (`Azorimor/linux-dualsense-fw-updater`) is an unofficial, community-maintained Linux desktop utility built with Rust and KDE Kirigami (Qt 6) for inspecting DualSense controller hardware and flashing firmware updates over a wired USB connection. It has **no affiliation, endorsement, or relation to Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation**.

**Unofficial Linux DualSense Firmware Updater** is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 or later (`GPL-3.0-or-later`)** and follows the FSFE REUSE specification. Full license texts live in `LICENSES/GPL-3.0-or-later.txt` and `LICENSES/MIT.txt`.
**Update** — Streams downloads with safe pre-flash cancellation, writes firmware in 32 KiB blocks via Feature Report `0xF4`, polls status via `0xF5`, verifies, and finalizes.
**Updates are irreversible:** Once flashing begins, firmware upgrades are auto-committed by the DualSense controller even if verify and finalize steps do not run.
